title: Malawax (Somali Cardamom Crêpes)
changes_from_base: A blended, sweetened batter with cardamom, a single egg and half water, cooked in ghee until the edges crisp and turn lacy, then sprinkled with sugar instead of served with lemon.
summary: Soft, golden Somali crêpes lightly spiced with cardamom and sprinkled with sugar, best served warm straight from the pan.
equipment: medium non-stick crêpe pan, frying pan or cast-iron griddle

ingredients.item: caster sugar, plus more to serve
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Blend the 176 g flour, 240 ml milk, 1 egg, 50 g sugar, 1 tsp cardamom, ⅛ tsp salt and 240 ml water until smooth and pour into a bowl.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Lightly grease a pan with ghee on kitchen paper and heat over medium-high heat until well heated.

steps.title: Pour
steps.text: Ladle in about 80 ml batter and swirl into a thin round.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook until no longer runny and brown underneath, 1-2 min, or until it releases easily.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Drizzle with ½ tsp melted ghee, flip and cook for 20-30 s, until the edges crisp and small golden pockets appear.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Turn onto a plate and sprinkle with sugar to taste, then repeat, wiping ghee over the pan between crêpes.

tips: Blend the ground cardamom in with the batter so every crêpe gets an even, gentle spice.
Keep the pan well heated throughout so each crêpe cooks quickly and develops golden pockets.
Wipe a little ghee over the pan between crêpes rather than pouring in more.
Sugar each crêpe while it's still warm so it dissolves slightly into the surface.
storage: Best eaten straight away while warm and the edges are still crisp. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
